text: The choice of vector database determines your RAG system's scale, cost, and operational complexity. A system that works perfectly with Chroma on your laptop may need fundamental redesign when you move to production with 100,000 users. This lesson prevents that mistake. In this lesson, vector database is store embeddings and enable fast approximate nearest neighbor, ANN Search, finding the top-k closest vectors to a query vector out of millions or billions of stored vectors. The three most common choices for production RAG systems each have a different profile. Chroma is open source, runs locally with no API key, and requires zero infrastructure to start. It stores data on disk or in memory. Perfect for development, prototyping, and applications with up to approximately one million vectors. Weakness, no built-in replication, backup, or multi-tenant isolation. Running Chroma in production requires operational work, managing the server, backups, restarts. For teams without dedicated DevOps, this becomes a maintenance burden. Pinecone is a fully managed cloud vector database. You create an index via API, absurd vectors, and query, no server management. Scales to billions of vectors, paid service. Start a tier is free with limits, one index, 100 megabyte storage, 100,000 vectors. Production tier costs scale with vector count and query volume. The main advantage, Pinecone handles all operational concerns, availability, backups, scaling, so your team focuses on the application. The main disadvantage, cost and data leaving your infrastructure. SuperBase PGVector is a PostgreSQL extension that adds a vector data type and ANN search operators to a standard PostgreSQL database. If your application already uses SuperBase for user authentication, data storage, and row level security, adding vector search costs nothing extra and keeps all data in one place. PGVector supports up to approximately 2,000 vector dimensions and handles millions of vectors efficiently. For African startups building on SuperBase, the most common back end is a service used by Kenyan indie developers. PGVector is often the best first choice. Zero additional infrastructure, familiar SQL interface, and SuperBase's row level security handles multi-tenant data isolation out of the box. Key decision framework. Use Chroma for development. Use SuperBase PGVector if you are already on SuperBase or want a single database for all your data. Use Pinecone when you need guaranteed SLA are managing more than 5 million vectors or need enterprise multi-region deployment. Apply what you learn in this lesson and you will see results immediately. Your skills bear fruit.
